neighbours.label: ' too' in 'too late' (or a similar degree word before a lateness/earliness word)
fire: By the time the ambulance arrived, it was already too late to save him.
Don't wait until it's too late to start saving for retirement.
She apologised, but the damage was done and it was too late.
They realised too late that the bridge had been closed.
If you call after five, it will be too late to book a table.
Many patients see a doctor only when it is too late.
He tried to warn them, but his message came too late.
It is never too late to learn a new language.
quiet: By the time the ambulance arrived, the street was too crowded to park.
Don't buy the shoes if they are too small for your feet.
She apologised, but the soup was too salty to eat.
They realised the bridge was too narrow for the truck.
If you call after five, the line will be too busy to answer.
Many patients find the waiting room too cold in winter.
He tried to lift the box, but it was too heavy.
This coffee is far too hot to drink right now.

notes: Card: ' too' 20 of top 32, every top example 'too late'; one 'a little bit earlier'. The - pole is 'just in time'. Near misses use 'too' with other adjectives. Not probed.
